column1: # UNGRADABLE.tsv -- ipl: shipped files that CANNOT be graded as standalone programs, each named with the reason
# MEASURED against the oracle. THE PACKAGE LOCKDOWN (Lon 2026-09-06).
# ⛔⭐⭐ A REASON NAMES THE ORACLE, NEVER US -- and `AGREEMENT-CONTROL:` is the one marker that admits a clause
# about our own compiler (ceo CEO-541, 2026-09-10, on hq_T's ask; the arm is lib_inventory.sh's honesty check,
# fixture-gated as ARM 8b of test_gate_package_runners_print_the_inventory.sh). A program excluded because SCRIP
# fails it is A RED MOVED OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR: the score cannot fall when we fail, because failing is what
# removes the entry. TWO rows here name us anyway -- gincl/maccolor.icn and incl/lshade.icn -- and both are
# legitimate, because in both the ruling is entirely the ORACLE'S: Arizona icont refuses at the same line, and
# upstream's UNMODIFIED copy refuses identically. Our clause adds only that we agree, which is a CONTROL: it
# shows the row is not our own damage. THE TEST IT PASSES, and the one to apply before typing the marker: THE
# RULING MUST STAND UNCHANGED IF SCRIP WERE PERFECT AT EVERYTHING ELSE.
# ⛔ HOW TO WRITE ONE: state the oracle's verdict FIRST and on its own -- naming the oracle, not us -- then
# prefix our clause with `AGREEMENT-CONTROL:`. The arm reads the text BEFORE the marker: it must name the
# oracle and must NOT name us. A row that mentions us ahead of the marker is refused exactly as before (the
# arizona general/tpp.icn precedent -- a row citing BOTH is still refused), and so is a row whose ruling really
# does rest on our failure, however politely the marker is applied.
# ⛔ These stay IN the denominator (POPULATION LAW 2026-09-04): shipped, never graded, never counted as passed.
# ⛔ ALL.icn is NOT listed here and is NOT in the population: it is OUR OWN generated container, not a vendored
#    program. It contaminated this package's counts once already (hq_I 2026-09-05: `find -name '*.icn'` counted it,
#    publishing 852/221/308 where the truth is 851/220/307). The runner's cross-instrument identity check now
#    REFUSES rc=2 rather than publish a number when the container's accounting and the walk disagree.
# SCOPE OF THIS FILE: the 390 files with no `procedure main` -- library modules, exercised via `link`, never
# standalone. The gradable remainder (461 files WITH a main, of which 64 carry a .std) is progs/UNGRADED.tsv,
# seat07's row icon-ipl-851-run-graded-against-iconx-refs-and-cured-by-class. ⚠ 9 of the 461 mains live in
# procs/ -- a census that assumes "procs/ is all library" undercounts the gradable population by nine.
# REASON is uniform because the measurement is: zero `procedure main` in the file, and the oracle refuses to run
# it with "Run-time error 117 in startup code / missing main procedure" (spot-checked on procs/strings.icn,
# procs/lists.icn, gprocs/patutils.icn, gincl/vdefns.icn -- all four printed exactly that).
# ── APPENDED 2026-09-06 hq_I (CEO-316): the 186 mains outside progs/ + clock-dependent re-rulings.

It is deterministic given a clean cwd (agrees across four sub-second runs AND across a minute boundary when each run gets a fresh scratch copy). It is ungradable for a different and stronger reason: a pinned ref would encode the file list of progs/, which OUR OWN ref-cutting mutates -- every new NAME.std in progs/ changes gcomp's correct output, so the ref would break itself. The earlier 'differs across a minute' reading was MY measurement error: the probe ran shar and filexref in the SAME scratch directory first, and those write files into cwd, so gcomp was reading their litter.

The stale ref was DELETED in the same commit rather than left to grade the calendar. WORDED WITHOUT NAMING US ON PURPOSE: an earlier revision added the disclaimer 'not a <compiler> defect' and lib_inventory.sh REFUSED the whole file for it -- the guard greps the reason text for our name and sees SPELLING, not EFFECT, so a sentence saying the defect is NOT ours reads to it exactly like one saying it is.

Its documented job is the number of days between TODAY and a given date (header: 'calculates the number of days between the current date and the date specified'), so its correct output changes daily; source reads &date and &dateline. ⛔ RULED BY SOURCE-READ, NOT BY RUN: util_cut_icon_ipl_refs.sh classified it LIVE 'would mint' with a 4-byte ref reading 340, because every determinism arm it has -- four sub-second runs plus a minute-crossing pass -- can only falsify variation FASTER than its own observation window. Do not re-open this on the strength of a green census.

Retrieves a URL over HTTP; its output is a remote server's response. MEASURED, and NOT for the reason first assumed: this box HAS network access and the program runs rc=0 (it fetched a real 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found' from example.com), so the blocker is not a missing network -- it is that any ref would pin a third party's reply. util_cut_icon_ipl_refs.sh's own confirmation runs already disagree with each other on it (NONDETERMINISTIC, 'disagreed on confirmation run 1/3'), so the instrument and the ruling agree here.

column3: The result is the FILE, never stdout: strips CR from each named file by writing a temp and moving it back (source: outfile := open(temp,"w"||ms), write(outfile,line)). MEASURED against the oracle 2026-09-06 with a 13-byte CRLF fixture: rc=0 and stdout+stderr together are ZERO BYTES while the named file goes 13 -> 11 bytes (CRs gone). The instrument diffs combined stdout+stderr against a .std, so the only ref it can cut here is the 0-byte one this package refuses -- a green cell over a program whose entire job went unobserved.

The inverse of nocr and the same shape: adds CR to each named file via a temp (source: outfile := open(temp_name,"w"||ms)). MEASURED against the oracle 2026-09-06 with an 11-byte LF fixture: rc=0, stdout+stderr ZERO BYTES, the named file 11 -> 13 bytes with CRLF line ends. Nothing the instrument can observe distinguishes a correct run from one that did nothing.

Builds an index FILE for a gettext-format text-base (source: outfile := open(idxfile_name,"w"), write_index(infile,outfile)). MEASURED against the oracle 2026-09-06 on a gettext-format fixture (keys are '::'-prefixed lines, the format its own header documents): rc=0, stdout+stderr ZERO BYTES, and the whole result is a 26-byte xxxxxgttxt.IDX. ⛔ DO NOT GRADE IT ON ITS ERROR PATH: fed plain text instead, the same oracle prints 'No indexed items found.' at rc=1 -- 23 gradable bytes that pin the program's own complaint and grade nothing it is for.

Prints the RUNNING USER AND HOST as its first output line. MEASURED against the oracle 2026-09-06 on a local one-link page: rc=0 and the output opens 'From:\tsatirical@socrates', then 'root:', 'home:' -- box identity, not program behaviour, so a pinned ref passes only on the box that cut it. ⭐ STABLE IN TIME, VARIES IN SPACE: two earlier reasons for this row were both wrong (it does NOT need the network for this input, and it is byte-stable across runs), so a run-twice determinism check sees a well-behaved program and calls this ruling a mistake. Nobody can fix it by re-running.
